text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'us-west-2-spot-gpu' experiencing sustained queue growth and autoscaler errors. Queue length +12x in last 10m, GPU utilization 96%. Autoscaler failing with cloud API errors (QuotaExceeded / RateLimitExceeded). Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/ops/gpu-pool?orgId=1

amber-oncall: ack. I'm paging infra/runtime. Starting ad-hoc bridge — join if available. @ben-runtime @cara-sre @frank-ops @grace-cs

ben-runtime: looking at autoscaler logs. seeing repeated: "Compute API error: quotaExceeded - project quota (GPUS) reached" plus bursts of "PreemptibleInstanceTermination" for 6 instances at once. Also multiple 500s from cloud provider during node creation.

cara-sre: confirmed from metrics: inference-queue: from 80 -> 960 in 12m. Throttling fired (rate limiter) and clients reporting 429/503. pasted log snippet:

```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR autoscaler: createNodes failed: quotaExceeded (GPUS)
2026-03-15T14:03:05Z WARN runtime: pod inference-abc returning 429 to client id=acct-42 req=xyz
2026-03-15T14:05:32Z INFO scheduler: paced evictions - reducing batch job concurrency
```

devon-pm: any customer impact confirmed? priority customers?

grace-cs: received two tickets from Enterprise A and Platform B reporting timeouts and elongated latencies (ticket #INC-5812, INC-5814). CS says degraded throughput for realtime endpoints, a minority of requests timing out but important SLAs impacted. Sent initial status to customers.

frank-ops: trying manual scale to on-demand pool but cloud API returns quota/limit errors too. Command attempted:

```
gcloud compute instances create --accelerator type=nvidia-t4,count=1 --zone us-west2-a --project redwood-prod
```

response: "Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project". Also see intermittent 500s when creating non-spot nodes. Opening quota ticket now but earliest ETA unknown.

ben-runtime: immediate mitigations proposal:
- pause non-critical batch/eviction jobs (reduce synthetic load)
- enable per-customer concurrency caps for enterprise tenants
- route critical realtime traffic to small on-demand reserved pool (if nodes available)
- enable model fallback: switch heavy ensembles to quantized xqat-medium variant to reduce GPU memory and worker count

amber-oncall: applying pause for batch jobs (k8s job label=non-critical). Patch incoming. Also applying per-customer limits on the gateway.

cara-sre: patching HPA/queue throttles now. kubectl commands:

```
kubectl label jobs -l job-type=batch non-critical=true --overwrite
kubectl patch hpa inference-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2,"maxReplicas":20}}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy /routing/hotfix (ring=ops) initiated by amber-oncall. run_id=run_20260315_1152. Enabling fallback routing rules for realtime model class.

cara-sre: after throttles and routing change queue length dropped ~30% in 10m. But autoscaler still failing to add nodes: cloud API 500s and quota errors persist. Preemptions still happening — looks like spot eviction wave + insufficient fallback.

ben-runtime: I'm reducing autoscaler API fanout and introducing exponential backoff. Also going to open provider support SR and request capacity advisory. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/autoscaler/pull/458 (hotfix: backoff + fanout limit).

amber-oncall: manual scaling attempt to on-demand pool failed due to project GPU quota. Leaving note for quota escalation: contact cloud-quotas@redwood with SR# 987221. Bridge going to stand for now. Handoff scheduled in 30m to frank-ops.

frank-ops: taking handoff at +30. I'll continue manual scale attempts and coordinate with cloud support. If quota ETA >1h, fallback is to throttle lower-priority customers and extend the quantized fallback. Also will attempt cross-region routing to eu-west if latency acceptable for affected customers.

grace-cs: posting customer update now. Template used: "We are aware of degraded performance for realtime endpoints due to GPU capacity constraints. Our engineering team is actively mitigating; estimated remediation 60-90 minutes. We'll send another update in 30 minutes or when we have new info." Tickets: INC-5812, INC-5814.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV2. Pages escalated to on-call and exec channel.

ben-runtime: hotfix merged, rolling out to autoscaler (reduce parallel create calls from 8->2, add jitter/backoff). Also enabling conservative fallback route to on-demand pool per request if model size <= medium. Rollout id: autoscaler-hotfix-20260315-01.

cara-sre: autoscaler hotfix rolled to 60% of controllers. Error rate dropped from ~22%->6% on create calls. Cloud support responded: they saw a regional quota spike and are provisioning temporary capacity; provider filing incident. Two on-demand nodes were successfully provisioned and joined cluster. Queue backlog trending down. 95th latency still elevated for heavy-model requests.

amber-oncall: summarizing for handoff to frank-ops:
- symptoms: spot eviction + quota spikes caused autoscaler failures -> queue growth -> throttling/429s
- impact: degraded realtime latency for subset of enterprise customers, tickets INC-5812/4
- actions taken: paused non-critical batch workloads, applied gateway per-customer caps, enabled quantized model fallback, deployed autoscaler backoff hotfix, opened cloud SR 987221, notified customers
- next steps: frank to continue cloud coordination, consider cross-region overflow routing, prepare detailed postmortem

frank-ops: ack. I'll keep bridge open for the next 45m and confirm when backlog < threshold. If provider can't deliver enough on-demand capacity, we'll work with product to schedule capacity reservations for peak windows.

deploy-bot: routing/hotfix run_id=run_20260315_1152 completed successfully.

cara-sre: 60m after initial page: queue at 110 (target <50), GPU utilization 78%, autoscaler create error rate <1%. Observability notes saved in runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/incidents/1739999999

amber-oncall: closing active bridge and handing off to frank-ops. Leaving link to logs, PRs, and cloud SR in the channel. Will follow up on postmortem.

frank-ops: taking over. I'll keep monitoring and loop in quotas and sales for customers affected.

amber-oncall: thanks team. Postmortem owners: cara-sre + ben-runtime. CS will own customer follow-ups.

incident-bot: Bridge closed by amber-oncall.
